content: Post-holiday QBR with VP Data Science and Infrastructure Director. Review of Q4 surge performance: capacity hit 94% utilization, 3 training jobs failed during peak, inference latency spiked 40%. Agreement that Q4 was barely manageable.

Capacity utilization normalizes to 62% as holiday traffic subsides. Compute Hour Consumption Trend drops 25% MoM. GPU utilization settles at 58%. Baseline workloads are recommendation model retraining (weekly) and demand forecasting inference (continuous).

CSM runs historical pattern analysis across 3 years of utilization data. Clear seasonal pattern emerges: capacity ramps 35-40% every Q4, with peak sustained for 10 weeks. Current infrastructure cannot support another year of growth on top of the seasonal spike.

Platform signal analyst flags seasonal capacity risk: 3-year trend shows 38% average Q4 compute surge with 6% YoY growth. At current trajectory, Q4 will require 130% of installed capacity. Expansion Probability jumps from 35% to 52%.

CSM presents seasonal capacity forecast to VP Data Science and Infrastructure Director. VP Data Science confirms: their internal demand model for new recommendation engine v3 and real-time personalization will add 15% on top of the seasonal spike. Combined demand: 145% of current capacity.

Joint capacity planning workshop completed. Infrastructure Director validates hardware requirements: 2 additional GPU racks (64 GPUs), upgraded cooling for sustained load, and network fabric expansion. Total expansion cost estimated at $1.6M. VP Data Science agrees to champion the budget request.

VP Data Science presents expansion proposal to CFO. CFO pushback: wants to see ROI analysis comparing proactive expansion vs. on-demand spot capacity. Requests cost-of-inaction analysis. Budget Availability Signals drop to 45 as CFO signals caution.

CSM produces comprehensive ROI deck: proactive expansion at $1.6M vs. emergency spot capacity at $2.4M (50% premium) plus $800K SLA penalty risk from degraded performance during surge. Net savings of proactive approach: $1.6M over 2 years. Infrastructure Director flags 12-week procurement lead time -- decision needed by week 22.

Early seasonal signals appear: Compute Hour Consumption begins trending upward 8% MoM as pre-holiday product development ramps. GPU utilization creeps from 58% to 63%. Training job queue times increasing. The surge is starting earlier than last year.

CSM escalates procurement timeline risk to VP Data Science: 4 weeks remain before the decision window closes. Health score dips to 65 as capacity planning uncertainty weighs on the account. VP Data Science arranges urgent CFO follow-up.

CFO approves $1.6M expansion budget. Key factors: CSM's ROI analysis showing $800K in avoided emergency costs, VP Data Science championing the investment, and early seasonal demand signals confirming the forecast. Purchase orders issued for 2 GPU racks, cooling upgrades, and network fabric expansion.

First GPU rack (32 GPUs) delivered and installation begins. Infrastructure Director oversees deployment with minimal disruption to production workloads. Cooling system upgrades completed in parallel. Capacity utilization drops to 52% as new capacity comes online before demand ramps.

First rack fully operational and validated. VP Data Science migrates recommendation engine v3 training to new GPUs. GPU utilization on new rack reaches 45% within first week. Training Job Completion Rate holds strong at 94%. Health score recovers to 75.

Second GPU rack (32 GPUs) installed and operational. Full expansion capacity online with 2 weeks to spare before surge period. Combined fleet: 192 GPUs with N+1 cooling. Load testing confirms system can sustain 95% utilization without thermal or performance degradation. Health score reaches 78.

Q4 surge begins. Compute Hour Consumption jumps 18% in first 2 weeks. Real-time personalization workloads for Black Friday preparation drive GPU utilization to 72% across expanded fleet. On old infrastructure this would have been 108% -- impossible without failures. System Uptime holds at 99.95%.

Black Friday / Cyber Monday peak. GPU utilization hits 88% on expanded fleet -- the highest sustained load in account history. All 47 concurrent training jobs complete successfully. Inference latency P95 holds at 38ms despite 3x normal traffic. Zero SLA breaches. VP Data Science calls it the smoothest holiday season in 4 years.

Mid-surge executive review with CFO. CSM presents real-time ROI dashboard: $800K in emergency spot capacity costs avoided, zero SLA penalties (vs. $200K estimated penalty exposure), and 100% training job completion during peak. CFO acknowledges the proactive investment thesis is validated.

Surge period concludes. Final scorecard: 10 weeks of sustained high demand, zero downtime, zero SLA breaches, 100% training job completion, $800K emergency costs avoided. Health score at 82, highest in account history. CFO initiates conversation about extending the predictive capacity planning model to other seasonal patterns.
